Signal bus / live synthesis telemetry

01 / Track worlds

Track-specific 16-step groove detection · original recording-derived micro-slices

02 / Signal → sculpture

Grain events influence geometry, reverb extends halos, envelope energy articulates faces, and percussion makes pulse rings.

03 / Performance · touch and motion

Three scene-adapted sound gestures plus a continuous, visual XY controller. Both axes change the same native DSP parameters as FM-1 encoder E2 (grain density) and E4 (motion). Appearance follows the sound-generated telemetry.

← SLOW MOTIONFAST MOTION →
↓ DENSE GRAINS↑ SPARSE GRAINS

MOTION 64 · DENSITY 64 · tuned for native FM-1 controls

05 / Original Melt with Miami source decks

Eight approximately four-bar source excerpts from six of your uploaded original WAV recordings. Sound can be looped, layered, speed-shifted and mixed with the native synth; the FM-1 carries shorter micrograin slices, not these complete browser samples.

Click Start audio to enable sample playback.

04 / Assignable audio + visual patchbay

6 routes per bank · 4 banks per scene · 8 scenes. Each connects one measured audio source or LFO to one synthesis or image destination, with signed depth and slew. SCL on hardware toggles patch editing.

Native matrix synchronized

05 / Play / MIDI test

Press and hold notes. Keyboard: A S D F G H J K. The exported binary renderer is the same C code as the FM-1 host firmware.

Visual and tonal reference to Daft Punk including Rolling & Scratching, Human After All, Within, Aerodynamic. No copyrighted samples, transcriptions, or recognizable melodies are embedded.
Independent synthesis: no protected songs, samples, film dialogue, or score transcriptions in this package. Hardware display preview uses the native 240×240 RGB565 engine; firmware flashing requires the manufacturer-compatible toolchain and on-device verification.
